title: Kafka will finally make sense after this video

idea.title: Kafka will finally make sense after this video
idea.aha: Kafka isn't a queue, it's an append-only log file, and each consumer just keeps a bookmark of how far it has read.
idea.pain: Your team adopted Kafka, and you're nodding along to 'partitions', 'offsets' and 'consumer groups' without knowing what they are.
didntKnow: Reading a message doesn't remove it; messages are deleted by age or size, read or not
Order is only guaranteed within one partition, not across a topic
A consumer group can't have more active consumers than partitions; the extra ones sit idle
You can replay the past by moving your offset back
A message's key decides its partition, which is how 'all events for user 42 stay in order' works
idea.visual: A long tape of numbered cells (the log) with bookmark arrows for each consumer; topic = several tapes side by side
idea.device: Bookmark arrows labelled with offset numbers that move along the log
idea.why: Directly matches the proven Redis/Nginx 'finally make sense' hit pattern with a top-searched tool
